Greenhorn
GREEN-horn
noun (Americana)
Formed within English by compounding green and horn, per the Oxford English Dictionary, which records its earliest evidence for the word in 1455. The OED lists uses in military contexts from the mid-1600s and for animals from the 1870s.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

A greenhorn is a raw beginner: a man new to a trade, a place or a way of life, and easily taken in. The word is an old English compound of green, the colour of what is fresh and unripe, and horn. It is far older than the American frontier, where it became a stock word for the newcomer from the East. The Christian observation: Scripture has no contempt for the beginner, only for the beginner who will not learn. “A wise man will hear, and will increase learning” (Pro 1:5), and “Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser” (Pro 9:9). But the green man is not to be put in charge too soon: an elder must be “Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil” (1Ti 3:6).

Webster 1828 Definition

A raw, inexperienced newcomer, easily deceived; from green + horn (OED earliest 1455). Not a novice in office (1Ti 3:6).

expand to see more

GREENHORN, n. (from 1455, OED) An inexperienced person; a newcomer unfamiliar with local ways and easily imposed upon. Compound of green + horn.

Key Scripture

Pro 1:5 — "A wise man will hear, and will increase learning; and a man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels:"

Pro 9:9 — "Give instruction to a wise man, and he will be yet wiser: teach a just man, and he will increase in learning."

1Ti 3:6 — "Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil."

Pro 14:15 — "The simple believeth every word: but the prudent man looketh well to his going."

Modern Corruption

Every man starts green; the danger is the greenhorn who is given authority before he has learned, or who refuses to learn because he thinks he already knows.

expand to see more

Paul set a plain rule for the church: no novice in office (1Ti 3:6). The reason is not that beginners are worthless but that early promotion feeds pride. A congregation that hands its pulpit or its board to the newest enthusiast has forgotten the rule.

The beginner has his own temptation, which is to believe whatever he is told: “The simple believeth every word” (Pro 14:15). The cure for being green is the word of God, which “giveth understanding unto the simple” (Psa 119:130).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

green (unripe) + horn → greenhorn (OED earliest 1455) → raw newcomer, easily deceived.
